title: 2022年9月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
paperTitle: 2022年9月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
passage:
P1 Academic dishonesty is nothing new. As long as there have been homework assignments and tests, there have been cheaters. The way that cheating looks has changed over time, though, particularly now that technology has made it easier than ever. A study by the Josephson Institute of Ethics interviewed 23,000 high school students and asked them a variety of questions about academic ethics. Of the teens surveyed, 51 percent said that they had knowingly cheated at some point on an exam but that they did not feel uneasy about the behavior. A Common Sense Media survey found that 35 percent of students had cheated via smartphone, though the parents surveyed in that particular study did not believe their kids had ever cheated. In many cases, students did not realize that strategies like looking up answers on a smartphone were actually cheating at all.

P2 In today's classrooms, students who cheat are rarely caught. There are no formulas written on the insides of hands or students looking across the aisle, or whispering answers to their classmates. Today's students use smartphones, tablets or even in-class computers to aid their cheating attempts and leave no trace of their crimes. Since cheating through technology is not listed specifically as being against the rules in many school policies, students do not view the actions as unethical.

P3 The technology is being adopted so quickly that school districts cannot adequately keep up with cheating policies, or even awareness campaigns that alert students to the problem with using technology to find answers in a certain way. From a young age, students learn that answers exist conveniently at their fingertips through search engines and expert websites.

P4 Schools must develop anti-cheating policies that include technology and these policies must be updated consistently. Teachers must stay on guard when it comes to what their students are doing in classrooms and how technology could be playing a negative role in the learning process. Parents must also talk to their kids about the appropriate ways to find academic answers and alert them to unethical behaviours that may seem innocent in their own eyes.

questions.q: What do we learn from the study by the Josephson Institute of Ethics?
options: Over half of the students interviewed were unaware they were cheating.
Cheating was becoming a way of life for a majority of high school teens.
More than half of the interviewees felt no sense of guilt over cheating.
Cheating was getting more and more difficult for high school students.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from the study 是对某项具体研究内容的客观转述提问,不涉及推断、主 旨、态度,属于针对单一信息源的细节题。

【拆句】结构是 What do we learn from the study by the Josephson Institute of Ethics?——主 干是 what do we learn from + 名词短语,介词短语 by the Josephson Institute of Ethics 修饰 the study,语序简单、无陷阱。 46. What do we learn from the study by the Josephson Institute of Ethics? A) Over half of the students interviewed were unaware they were cheating. B) Cheating was becoming a way of life for a majority of high school teens. C) More than half of the interviewees felt no sense of guilt over cheating. D) Cheating was getting more and more difficult for high school students.

【定位】Of the teens surveyed, 51 percent said that they had knowingly cheated at some point on an exam but that they did not feel uneasy about the behavior. 在受访的青少年中,51% 的人说他们曾在某次考试中明知故犯地作弊,但对这种行为并不感到 不安。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 Over half of the students interviewed were unaware they were cheating. 说"过半 受访者不知道自己在作弊",但定位句明明用了 knowingly,与之相反;"不知情作弊"是后文 Common Sense Media 部分讨论的内容,被偷换到本题。 B) 过度推断 Cheating was becoming a way of life for a majority of high school teens. 把"曾在 某次考试作弊"升级为"成为生活方式",程度被无端拔高;定位句只说"曾经作弊过",并未 说"已成为日常"。 C) ✓ 正确 51 percent said that they had knowingly cheated ↔More than half of the interviewees did not feel uneasy about the behavior ↔felt no sense of guilt over cheating More than half of the interviewees felt no sense of guilt over cheating. 把"过 半"和"无负罪感"同时对上定位句,正是细节题最干净的同义替换。 D) 与原文相反 Cheating was getting more and more difficult for high school students. 说作弊 变得越来越难,但全文核心论点是 technology has made it easier than ever,方向完全 相反。 Common Sense Media 的调查揭示了什么? A) 大多数家长倾向于过度保护自己的孩子。 B) 许多学生在不知情的情况下作弊。 C) 学生迫切需要道德教育。 D) 家长和孩子对作弊的看法存在冲突。

questions.q: What did the Common Sense Media survey reveal?
options: Most parents tended to overprotect their children.
Many students committed cheating unknowingly.
Students were in urgent need of ethical education.
Parents and kids had conflicting ideas over cheating.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did the Common Sense Media survey reveal? 同样指向某项具体调查的客观发现, 属于客观转述,不涉态度/推断。

【拆句】What did the Common Sense Media survey reveal?——主谓宾极简单,reveal 在此当及 物动词"揭示",一个主语一个宾语,无修饰、无从句。 47. What did the Common Sense Media survey reveal? A) Most parents tended to overprotect their children. B) Many students committed cheating unknowingly. C) Students were in urgent need of ethical education. D) Parents and kids had conflicting ideas over cheating.

【定位】A Common Sense Media survey found that 35 percent of students had cheated via smartphone, though the parents surveyed in that particular study did not believe their kids had ever cheated. In many cases, students did not realize that strategies like looking up answers on a smartphone were actually cheating at all. Common Sense Media 的一项调查发现 35% 的学生曾用智能手机作弊,尽管该项调查中受 访的家长并不相信自己的孩子曾经作弊。很多情况下,学生根本没意识到用手机查答案这种做 法其实就是作弊。

【选项】A) 无中生有 Most parents tended to overprotect their children. 中 overprotect(过度保护)是原 文里完全没出现的概念,文中只说家长 did not believe their kids had ever cheated(不 相信孩子作过弊),这是"不知情"而非"过度保护"。 B) ✓ 正确 students did not realize that strategies like looking up answers on a smartphone were actually cheating at all ↔Many students committed cheating unknowingly looking up answers on a smartphone were actually cheating ↔committed cheating Many students committed cheating unknowingly. 同时覆盖"作弊"和"不自知"两个要 点,正是定位句最干净的同义替换。 C) 答非所问 Students were in urgent need of ethical education. 是"应该"层面的建议(末段才有类 似主张),并非该调查所揭示的事实;47 题问的是 reveal,要求是事实,不是该做什么。 D) 偷换概念 Parents and kids had conflicting ideas over cheating. 把家长不知情与学生不自知放 在一起描述为"观念冲突",但原文里两方都不认为自己/孩子在作弊,实际上是"双方都没认 识到",不是冲突,而是同向盲区。 为什么现在学生很少因作弊被抓? A) 他们把公式抄在手掌上。 B) 他们互相帮助掩盖自己的行为。 C) 他们不断改变作弊方式。 D) 他们利用现代技术。

questions.q: Why do students rarely get caught cheating nowadays?
options: They copy formulas on their palms.
They help each other to cover up their acts.
They keep changing their ways of cheating.
They make use of modern technology.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why do students rarely get caught cheating nowadays? 用 Why 问原因,但原因往往在 原文同一句或紧邻句给出,不需多步推理,仍属细节定位。 48. Why do students rarely get caught cheating nowadays? A) They copy formulas on their palms. B) They help each other to cover up their acts. C) They keep changing their ways of cheating. D) They make use of modern technology.

【拆句】Why do students rarely get caught cheating nowadays?——副词 rarely 是隐性否 定"很少/几乎不",get caught doing 是"被抓到正在做某事"的固定结构,nowadays 限定时 间。基础薄弱考生注意:rarely 不是"罕见"的名词,而是"很少"的副词。

【定位】In today's classrooms, students who cheat are rarely caught. There are no formulas written on the insides of hands or students looking across the aisle, or whispering answers to their classmates. Today's students use smartphones, tablets or even in-class computers to aid their cheating attempts and leave no trace of their crimes. 在今天的教室里,作弊的学生很少被抓到。没人再在手心写公式、隔着过道偷看,或者向同学 小声报答案。今天的学生用智能手机、平板,甚至课堂电脑辅助作弊,不留任何痕迹。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 They copy formulas on their palms. 实际上正是原文用 no formulas written on the insides of hands 否定掉的旧做法,选项把这条已经被否定的现象当成"现在"还在做,方向 恰好反了。 B) 无中生有 They help each other to cover up their acts. 中 cover up(掩盖)的描述在原文里完全 没有;原文只说技术让作弊"不留痕迹",并未说学生互相帮忙打掩护。 C) 偷换概念 They keep changing their ways of cheating. 描述"学生不断改变作弊方式",但原文 是"作弊方式随时代而变"——主语是"作弊方式",不是"学生";而且 keep changing 强调 持续变化,原文只比较了"以前 vs 现在"两个时点。 D) ✓ 正确 use smartphones, tablets or even in-class computers ↔They make use of modern technology to aid their cheating attempts ↔make use of They make use of modern technology. 用 modern technology 一词覆盖原文三种设 备,且对应了 to aid their cheating attempts 的"借助"语义,是干净的概括化替换。 作者认为学校应该如何应对作弊? A) 更新反作弊政策使其跟上时代。 B) 不断改革考试方法。 C) 利用最新技术。 D) 提醒家长注意孩子的行为。

questions.q: What does the author think schools should do to tackle cheating?
options: Bring policies against cheating up to date.
Reform their exam methods constantly.
Take advantage of the latest technologies.
Alert parents to their children's behaviour.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author think schools should do 问的是作者对学校的具体建议,原文末段 是直接的祈使/must 句,属客观陈述,不是推断。 49. What does the author think schools should do to tackle cheating? A) Bring policies against cheating up to date. B) Reform their exam methods constantly. C) Take advantage of the latest technologies. D) Alert parents to their children's behaviour.

【拆句】What does the author think schools should do to tackle cheating?——主句 What does the author think,后接宾语从句 schools should do,不定式 to tackle cheating 作目 的状语,逻辑就是"作者认为学校该做什么来解决作弊"。

【定位】Schools must develop anti-cheating policies that include technology and these policies must be updated consistently. 学校必须制定包含科技因素的反作弊政策,并且这些政策必须不断更新。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 these policies must be updated consistently ↔Bring policies against cheating up to date anti-cheating policies ↔policies against cheating Bring policies against cheating up to date. 把"持续更新政策"这一并列要点提炼 出来,正命中原文 must be updated consistently;且 against cheating 等值替换 anti-cheating。 B) 无中生有 Reform their exam methods constantly. 提到"改革考试方式",但原文末段对学校的建 议只涉及"制定/更新政策",未谈考试方式的改革。 C) 与原文相反 Take advantage of the latest technologies. 让学校利用最新技术(去解决作弊),但原文 里技术是问题源——students learn that answers exist conveniently at their fingertips through search engines——学校要做的是把技术纳入政策约束,而非利用技 术解决问题。 D) 张冠李戴 Alert parents to their children's behaviour. 让学校去提醒家长,但原文末段对学 校只字未提家长这件事;"alert"一词原文里出现在家长对孩子的位置 alert them to unethical behaviours。 作者建议教师在课堂上做什么? A) 防止学生过度使用电子设备。 B) 制定更有效的反作弊策略。 C) 寻找更多方法遏制学生的不道德行为。 D) 防范学生滥用技术。

questions.q: What does the author suggest teachers do in the classroom?
options: Prevent students from overusing electronic devices.
Develop more effective anti-cheating strategies.
Find more ways to curb students' unethical acts.
Guard against students' misuse of technology.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author suggest teachers do in the classroom? 仍是对原文一句建议句的 转述,无推断需求,属细节题。 50. What does the author suggest teachers do in the classroom? A) Prevent students from overusing electronic devices. B) Develop more effective anti-cheating strategies. C) Find more ways to curb students' unethical acts. D) Guard against students' misuse of technology.

【拆句】What does the author suggest teachers do in the classroom?——suggest 后接省略 that 的宾语从句 teachers (should) do,基础薄弱考生注意:suggest 后从句的 should 常省 略,do 是动词原形而不是名词。

【定位】Teachers must stay on guard when it comes to what their students are doing in classrooms and how technology could be playing a negative role in the learning process. 老师必须时刻警惕——既要警惕学生在课堂里都在做什么,也要警惕科技可能在学习过程中 扮演的负面角色。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 Prevent students from overusing electronic devices. 把"科技扮演负面角色"窄化为 单一的"过度使用电子设备";原文要警惕的核心不是"用得太多",而是"用得不当"(作弊)。 B) 张冠李戴 Develop more effective anti-cheating strategies. 让老师去"制定更有效的反作弊策 略",但末段把"develop policies"的任务给了 schools,老师只是"stay on guard"。 C) 过度推断 Find more ways to curb students' unethical acts. 让老师"找出更多办法去遏制不道德 行为",但原文里老师的动作只是"警惕",并未要求老师去找新办法或主动出击。 D) ✓ 正确 Teachers must stay on guard ↔Guard against how technology could be playing a negative role in the learning process ↔ students' misuse of technology Guard against students' misuse of technology. 把"警惕"与"科技的负面作用"两块拼 成一个干净的动宾结构,正命中原文要点。
